searchText: Should we begin the deprecation process of Goerli? i think instead we start a push to migrate ppl to sepolia don't need to touch goerli substantially immediately having pushed people to move to goerli this past year, I'd like to see "one last thing" we do to keep things manageable for the next year-ish as we transition i think we need a commitment that goerli's time is limit and big projects need to begin looking at migrating -- my understanding is a lot of ppl test on goerli bc it has the deployments for uniswap, opensea, etc already I wouldn't call it deprecation, just "don't fix the goETH supply issue". i think it needs to be deprecation because the "don't fix the goETH supply issue" will just accelerate it's path toward a paid testnet if infura and validators spin down, goerli is effectively dead - so we should make a commitment that that is coming at some point in the future I think if we want to shut down Goerli, we need both broad infra support for Sepolia (it's starting, but not quite on par with Goerli yet) as well as a reliable validator testnet Paid testnet != dysfunctional/offline/not-working testnet. it sounds like we are getting rolling ephemeral staking testnets to micah's point, we could move most testing to sepolia, have ephemeral staking testnets and *still* have a "paid" testnet simply bc we didn't do anything to goerli there _is_ space for an incentivized testnet I think if we want to make Goerli an incentivized testnet, it should be an explcit commitment to the extent "we" can make one Why do you think that is necessary? A lot of testnet infra exists with the assumption GoETH is free I'm still struggling to understand why the current situation is a problem. e.g. faucets if it becomes paid, you basically lose all that What is the sad user story here? ppl want to use goerli for testing and cant I also think making it paid means all the bots/faucet drainers of the past year "win" there simply is not liquid goETH available so we're rewarding everyone who was "smart enough" to drain all the faucets, making the experience worse for literally everyone else I *think* my argument against your position (though maybe not since I'm not totally clear on your position) is that we shouldn't care so much about people who are building stuff that depends on Infura to work. We should be focusing our efforts on supporting dapp developers who run their own software, and encourage their users to do the same. that seems like a bit of a sunk cost fallacy, assuming we have upgrade paths like i mentioned above to new testnets (re tim's last message) I think GoETH being valuable will also make Goerli stickier then people have a vested interest in keeping it around - that might be OK if we _want_ an incentivized testnet. It doesn't feel like that's something core devs ever wanted though (as we didn't create one), so I'm more uneasy with Goerli morphing into that than if, say, we created an incentivized testnet from scratch I don't understand how Infura relates to this 🤔 ? I *think* you are saying that "existing infrastructure uses goerli", which I'm interpreting to mean "centralized stuff like Infura". Anyone who is building actually censorship resistant software should have zero problem moving to Sepolia. ha, right fair The only reason one would want to stay on Goerli is because either you need to integrate with a bunch of stuff that is on Goerli (network effects are strong), or because your software relies on centralized infrastructure that only supports Goerli. For the latter case, I don't care to support those people. For the former case, I think we *want* to give weak incentives to start migrating to Sepolia specifically because strong network effects make the process slow. In our current paradigm, Goerli is our only public way to test being a validator before doing it on mainnet. Plenty of staking providers use it as a form of staging before mainnet. We have plans for ephermeral testnets, etc - but we don't know if they work. So our current only option is to keep goerli alive as a service we provide to the staking community. They can't migrate away at all, dapp devs can and probably should. We could probably drop some sep.ETH to dapps that we can identify on goerli, to make it easier for them to move? We have much lower supply constraints anyway Even if we deprecate goerli and have sepolia as the only testnet, we'd still need to solve the problem of having a really large beaconchain in order to ensure we don't deploy things that can't work at mainnet size. So either we'd need another testnet or we can find a way to keep goerli around. One other factor here is that we haven't been able to add validators to goerli fast enough to keep up with mainnet which reduces its usefulness as a testnet for consensus client devs testing as well. Periodically starting new testnets for validators to test on, with as many validators as we care to shove into the genesis state, would make it much easier to keep up with mainnet validator count. Which is Pari's last point now I read it properly. 🙂 I guess we lack the history aspect of the long chain but that doesn't matter as much in my mind. Large world state does make a difference for ELs but that will grow on Sepolia as dapps move over and time progresses. The one thing we lose with launching new testnets for CL teams is the non trivial topology of the network. I'd suspect that Goerli is more useful with less validators than a testnet with twice as many validators concentrated in 4 clusters True, I'd say both large validator set and distributed are very useful. Goerli is well behind mainnet on both counts these days though. That said, distribution would be a lot worse if dapps weren't running on the testnet since you basically wouldn't have any non-validating nodes.
